question: Can the two identified hung processes be retired now, as explicitly requested, while preserving all six recoverable experiments?
hypothesis: Identity-checked process termination may release the two stale GPU contexts while healthy peers continue. Checkpoint snapshots preserve a recovery path if the device is affected; successful teardown does not identify the original fault.

sources.sections: General checkpoint for resuming training, multiple models, GPU checkpoint loading on CPU
sources.consequence: Preflight all saved components against the original implementation, preserving the source artifact. A weights-only load is insufficient for resumption.

sources.sections: Reproducibility limitations, RNGs and nondeterministic algorithms
sources.consequence: Restore CPU/GPU RNG and retain the same environment and deterministic per-epoch/per-step seeds. Do not promise bitwise identity or change backend determinism settings mid-experiment.

sources.version: current official documentation read 2026-11-15; installed psutil 7.2.2
sources.sections: Process identity, is_running, terminate, kill and wait
sources.consequence: Bind any approved process action to PID plus creation time and command/cwd. Treat zombies and absent processes distinctly; never signal a reused PID.

On the same GPU model, a different runtime/workload reports device resets during hung-process teardown. Wait until healthy peers finish and their final artifacts are preserved before any process cleanup. This report does not diagnose our hang or authorize its workaround.

differences: Supersedes only the deferred execution proposal in A005. User explicitly prefers killing the two hung processes now rather than waiting for healthy peers; accepts checkpoint recovery if other work is interrupted. A005 CPU preparation remains valid and is retained unchanged. No change to scientific data/configuration or model code.
contrary_evidence: The same-GPU firsthand report describes a reset on hung-process teardown. Our four progressing peers and lack of kernel errors do not establish that teardown is safe. Checkpoints cannot preserve unsaved updates.

protocol.authorization: User: I would rather we killed the two hung processes, worst case we can restart all3 from the checkpoints. Apply to PIDs2407193 and2407195 only; healthy jobs receive no signals. Retiring the obsolete waiting A003 CPU queue is necessary to prevent an evaluation race.
protocol.preservation: Before signals, copy latest full checkpoints, configs, metrics and logs for all six original runs through open inodes; CPU-verify steps, configuration and finite state, and record hashes. Preserve queue manifest/state/log and verify pinned source hashes.
protocol.cleanup: Confirm PID/create_time/command/cwd and stale target step immediately before each action. Stop waiting queue2425797 first and confirm exit. Send SIGTERM to the two specified trainers; allow30 seconds for exit, then one identity-checked SIGKILL if required. Record actions and outcomes. No GPU reset, reboot, runtime/driver changes or signals to healthy trainers.
protocol.observation: Read kernel/GPU telemetry and all original process/step histories before and after. Observe healthy step advancement at least60 seconds after cleanup. CPU busy alone is not progress. Review outcome against primary sources before recovery.
protocol.continuation: Original experiments may resume from preserved full state under the unchanged pinned trainer, one replacement at a time, with exact source/data/config lineage and review before each dependent action. If healthy peers survive, finish them before serial replacement training. If device-wide failure interrupts peers, prepare continuation for affected runs from latest intact checkpoints; device-level repair needs a separate reviewed decision. Replace old queue with explicit six-run final-path resolution and unchanged A003 checks after all final artifacts exist.
protocol.checks: No overwritten original evidence; exact process identities; queue exited before trainer cleanup; all checkpoints load on CPU and remain finite; surviving useful progress recorded. Preparation alone is not numerical/scientific success.

success: Both target contexts exit and four peers continue advancing; otherwise record exact collateral impact and preserved recovery state. Later continuation completion and A003 validity are separate gates.
stop: Stop escalation after bounded signals or on identity mismatch/device fault. No automatic device reset or repeated restart loop. Never declare a model failure from a runtime hang.

resources.training_device: none during cleanup; future original-training continuation accounted separately as in A005
